1  Dated this the 7th day of August 2025
JUDGMENT

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.1/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 24/08/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the second respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 09/10/2016 at about 09:45 p.m., while she was pillion riding on motorcycle bearing registration no.KL05-U-6517 driven by the first respondent and when she reached Thrissur-Ernakulam sector at Potta signal junction, the first respondent dozed off as a result of which he lost 2025:KER:59268 MACA NO. 463 OF 2020 control of the motorcycle and it overturned due to which the claim petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The incident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the first respondent/owner-cum- rider of the motorcycle.
A sum of 5,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner-cum-rider remained ex parte.
4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle, but denied negligence on the part of the first respondent.

The age,
occupation and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A11 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner and Ext.B1 was marked on the side of the second respondent/insurer.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part 2025:KER:59268 MACA NO. 463 OF 2020 of the first respondent/owner-cum-rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,36,792/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Compensation for permanent disability post retirement

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the Tribunal committed a gross error in fixing the notional income at 10,000/- when evidence has come on record to show that the claim petitioner while in Menon Leena C vs *United India Insurance Company ... on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48018590/
2 service was drawing an amount of 41,429/-.

sentences.text: Therefore, the notional income needs to be appropriately 2025:KER:59268 MACA NO. 463 OF 2020 enhanced.
Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the second respondent/insurer that the amount that has been fixed by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and that no enhancement is called for.
9.1. The fact that the claim petitioner was working as Accountant in the Kerala State Electricity Board is not disputed.
Ext.A10 salary certificate shows that she was drawing monthly income of 41,429/-.
Ext.A10 certificate was also accepted by the Tribunal.
That being so, the notional income for the purpose of computation of compensation for loss of earning power after retirement can be fixed as 20,000/-.
Therefore, the amount to which she would be entitled will be 2,37,600 /-, that is, 20,000 x 12 x 9 x 11/100.
Pain and suffering 10.

The materials on record show that following injuries were sustained by the claim petitioner:
"1) multiple abrasion both knees, (Rt) upper arm, (Rt) elbow, (Rt) hand, (Lt) elbow.
2) 5 x 1 cm laceration (Rt) forehead.
2025:KER:59268 MACA NO. 463 OF 2020 3) blunt chest trauma with fracture of 6th and 7th rib right 4) closed displaced humerus shaft fracture of right side."
The claim petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 8 days.
She also underwent a surgery.
Therefore, taking into account the injuries sustained, which include fractures also, I find that an amount of 65,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Loss of amenities 11.
Though an amount of 50,000/- was claimed under this head, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 20,000/- only, which is also stated to be on the lower side.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that an amount of 40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 1,63,800/- (total 2025:KER:59268 MACA NO. 463 OF 2020 compensation = 5,00,592/- that is,
3,36,792/- granted by the Tribunal plus 1,63,800/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization and proportionate costs.
The second respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
